description.narrative: By the end of 2023, in collaboration with social partners, MOL adopted as a pilot, a new tool ensuring better employment conditions for home-based care worker in alignment with the national labour law and inspired by convention 189. Through RBSA funded intervention WE CARE, ILO assisted the Ministry of Labour to develop a digital platform for job matching in the care sector, with a focus on home-based care. Employment conditions were integrated in the platform and are a condition for matching through the platform. Given the stagnating policy environment in Lebanon which delays efforts to include home-based care workers in the national labour law, integrating such conditions intends to pave the way to policy reform. ILO integrated Impact indicators in the digital platform to inform future interventions related to the protection of home-based workers and facilitated discussions with social partners on the platform.

title.narrative: 7.5.2. Number of Member States with new or improved services to protect the labour rights of migrant workers
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: In November 2022, the Kenyan Central Organization of Trade Unions (COTU-K) and the National Federation of Worker and Employee Trade Unions in Lebanon (FENASOL) signed an inter-union Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), to ensure a more solid protection framework for Kenyan workers travelling to (and returning from) Lebanon. The MOU commits to the principle of ensuring Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work and rights laid out in international labour standards for migrant workers, engages the unions to advocate for ratification of relevant Conventions and has a monitoring and review mechanism and at least three technical virtual meetings have been held between the two union federations in 2023. FENASOL has introduced a new service for migrant workers, staffed by a lawyer, which provides group legal counselling, individual case work as well as support and advice to migrant workers including for both legal and administrative requests (including relating to regularization of work permits, non-payment of wages, registration of children, etc.). Between December 2022 to July 2023, FENASOL has provided support to 279 women migrant workers (of whom 53 have been referred to other service providers/organizations). The ILO contributed to the development and implementation of the MOU by supporting and facilitating a mission to Lebanon in July 2022 by COTU-K. The mission included meeting with dozens of Kenyan domestic workers to hear their challenges and concerns and close discussions with FENASOL. These exchanges led the trade union federations to affirm their mutual support to work individually and at a corridor level to protect workers. The ILO continues to engage periodically with both federations to support ongoing implementation of the MOU. From December 2022 until December 2023, with support from the Government of Switzerland, ILO supported FENASOL to provide group legal counselling, individual case work, support and advice to migrant workers including for both legal and administrative requests such as regularization of work permits, non-payment of wages, registration of children, etc.
